# Use a standard Ubuntu base image, suitable for general-purpose CPU workloads.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation of packages.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, certificates, and OpenMPI.
# - build-essential: Includes C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
# - git: For cloning the source code repository.
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: The OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# We run all apt commands in a single layer to optimize image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce final image size.
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments like Kubernetes.
# This ensures MPI tasks communicate over the container network interface (e.g., eth0)
# rather than relying on shared memory mechanisms that may not work across pods.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Clone the AMG source code, build the dependency libraries, then the main
# executable, copy it to the PATH, and clean up the source.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /opt/amg && \
    # Explicitly build each required library first using a loop to resolve linker errors.
    # FIX: Use correct shell variable expansion ($dir instead of $$dir).
    for dir in utilities krylov IJ_mv seq_mv parcsr_mv parcsr_ls; do \
        (cd "/opt/amg/$dir" && make); \
    done && \
    # Now that libraries are built, compile the main executable in the 'test' directory.
    cd /opt/amg/test && make && \
    # Copy the compiled binary to a location on the system PATH.
    cp amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    # Remove the source code to minimize image size.
    rm -rf /opt/amg

# Set a default entrypoint or command. This can be overridden at runtime.
# For an HPC application, this is often the mpirun command itself.
# We provide a bash shell as a reasonable default for interactive use.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the AMG2023 benchmark on a single AWS CPU-based Kubernetes node.
# It is configured for a small-scale test run as requested.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg2023-test-aws-cpu
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (processes) for the job. Must be >= 4.
  tasks: 4

  # Ensure the job pods and services are not deleted upon completion to allow for log inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Fail on any encountered error.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute within the container.
      # The 'flux run' or 'flux submit' is implicitly added by the Flux Operator.
      # -problem 2: Specifies the exact problem set to run as required.
      # -n 4 4 4: Defines a small problem size (4x4x4 grid), suitable for testing.
      # -P 2 2 1: Sets the processor grid for the 4 tasks (2*2*1=4 tasks).
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4 -P 2 2 1

      # This is a worker container, not the main job launcher.
      # With only one container definition, this is standard.
      launcher: false

# This MiniCluster manifest is configured to run the AMG2023 benchmark on a memory-optimized AWS ARM64 instance.
# It attempts to resolve a container bootstrap issue by enabling Flux's minimal service mode.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2023-test-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster must run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is kept at 64 to match the vCPUs of the selected instance for debugging purposes.
  tasks: 64

  # Ensure the job pods and services are not deleted upon completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  flux:
    # The m7g is an ARM-based Graviton instance, requiring this specific flux-view image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
    # Enable minimal service mode to bypass the default bootstrap script which requires curl/wget,
    # as these tools are missing from the application container. This directly addresses the previous failure.
    minimalService: true

  # Pod spec additions to select the optimal node instance type.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # Continuing to use a high-resource instance to debug performance issues.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command runs the required problem with a small problem size for testing.
      # -problem 2: Specifies the exact problem set to run.
      # -n 4 4 4: Defines a small problem size (4x4x4 grid) for testing as requested.
      # -P 4 4 4: Sets the processor grid for the 64 tasks (4*4*4=64 tasks).
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4 -P 4 4 4
      # This is a worker container, not the main job launcher.
      launcher: false
